thread:
daniel_acme: Hey team — raising an escalation. Our embeddings endpoint is returning inconsistent vector sizes. Most calls return 1536-d vectors, but intermittently we get 768-d or an explicit error 'embedding dimensionality mismatch'. This spikes when we send batched requests from our worker pool.

sam_support: Sorry you're hitting this, daniel. Can you paste a minimal repro (request body + headers + response) and roughly how often it happens?

daniel_acme: Repro steps below. Occurs ~0.8-1.5% of requests.

```
# curl snippet we use
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: acme-1234-req-42" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","inputs":["doc1","doc2",...], "batch_size":16}'
```

Example failing response we logged: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error":"embedding dimensionality mismatch: expected 1536 got 768",
  "request_id":"acme-1234-req-42",
  "route":"/v1/embeddings"
}
```

Also saw plain vectors returned with length 768 in the raw body (no error).

jia_ml: Thanks for the repro. Two quick pieces to check: (1) is the model always the same variant (open-embed-1536) or do you sometimes route to a smaller quantized variant? (2) are you multiplexing different models over the same client instance?

sam_support: Also checking if batch boundary handling could be collapsing metadata between requests. Priya, any recent batching runtime changes?

priya_sre: Not that I'm aware of in prod, no global batching change in the last 2 weeks. But we did land a micro-optimization in the serializer for embeddings on 2026-03-01 on a few nodes. I'll correlate.

daniel_acme: Confirmed model param always 'open-embed-1536' from our side. No model multiplexing. We do have multiple workers doing concurrent requests though (each sends a batch of inputs per call).

observability-bot: Automated note: There are 47 trace spans with tag "embedding_dim_mismatch" in the last 24h for customer org "acme". Top host: gpu-node-13.

sam_support: Okay, next steps I recommend to isolate whether this is a runtime batching bug vs client-side mis-encoding: 
- Turn on per-request tracing for 5 minutes and send a filtered set of requests (single worker, reproducible batch size). Add header `X-Redwood-Trace: on`.
- If you can, also try sending same payload with `batch_size:1` to see if the issue disappears (this will rule out server-side batch merging bug).
- Share one raw failing trace id (from X-Request-ID) and we'll pull spans.

jia_ml: Helpful note: if the bug is in the batch coalescing logic, you'll see a trace with these spans in order: `receive -> batcher/merge -> model_infer -> serialize-> respond`. Dimension mismatches typically originate in `batcher/merge` or `serialize`. Look for inconsistent `vector_len` metadata on the span boundaries.

daniel_acme: I flipped `batch_size` to 1 for 1000 calls, and so far zero fails. With 16 it repros ~0.9% again. I collected one failing request id: acme-1234-req-2026-03-05-778

sam_support: Great, that's very telling. Can you also enable traces and share the trace id if you see it? I'm pulling logs for acme-1234-req-2026-03-05-778 now.

priya_sre: I pulled the runtime logs for that request id on gpu-node-13. Snippet: 
```
[2026-03-05T14:22:10.123Z] req=acme-1234-req-2026-03-05-778 span=batcher/merge info="merged 16 inputs" batch_id=b-998
[2026-03-05T14:22:10.456Z] req=acme-1234-req-2026-03-05-778 span=model_infer info="model open-embed-1536 returning shape=(16,1536)"
[2026-03-05T14:22:10.789Z] req=acme-1234-req-2026-03-05-778 span=serialize warn="serialized 16 vectors but observed serialized_length mismatch for item 7" detail="got 768 bytes for item7"
```

priya_sre: That warn is odd — model_infer reported (16,1536) then serializer claimed item 7 serialized to half-length. Possible memory corruption or chunking bug during serialization.

jia_ml: Could be an off-by-one in the GPU->CPU copy path when certain alignment occurs. We had a similar flake in staging when `max_batch_bytes` exceeded a threshold. Does your route have custom batching config?

daniel_acme: Our route uses default batching. We didn't touch max_batch_bytes.

sam_support: For immediate mitigation, please set the route override to disable batch coalescing for your customer: `batching.prefer_unbatched: true` or set `max_batch_size: 1` in the route config. This will increase per-request cost but should prevent the dim mismatch while we investigate.

priya_sre: I'll open a P0 on infra side to investigate the serializer path on gpu-node-13 and the recent micro-optimization. Jia, can you look at the serialization code and the AVX alignment patch we merged on 2026-03-01?

jia_ml: On it. Also adding additional assertions in the serializer to fail fast when shape metadata disagrees with bytes serialized. That will give better traces.

observability-bot: Tip: in Console -> Tracing, filter route=/v1/embeddings and add column `span_tags.vector_len` and `batch_id`. Group by `batch_id` -> sort by error rate. Also add a panel to the Embeddings dashboard: "per-request serialized_length vs expected_vector_len" to catch this quickly.

billing-bot: Noting: if you flip to unbatched, billing will show ~x4 increase in per-embedding compute costs. See console cost estimator.

daniel_acme: We've toggled `prefer_unbatched` and the failures stopped in our quick smoke run. We'll keep it for now. Thank you. Can you share ETA for a proper fix and whether this will require a restart of nodes?

priya_sre: ETA: triage complete in 2 hours, fix PR within the day if it's a serializer regression, rolling restart of affected host pool (gpu-node-13 and peers) potentially required. We'll post timeline here.

sam_support: I'll keep you updated and add a follow-up: once Jia's patch lands, we'll run a canary with batched traffic for a few hours. If all green, schedule a staggered rollout.

daniel_acme: Appreciate it. Can you also add a short dashboard alert for us (and us only) that triggers on >0.1% dim_mismatch errors over 5m so we can auto-promote to on-call?

observability-bot: You can create a Customer-scoped alert in Console -> Alerts -> New Alert using the metric `embedding_dim_mismatch.count` with a filter `customer_id:acme` and threshold 1 in 5m. Recommend action: auto-create ticket to support channel.

sam_support: Thanks everyone. Summary / action items: 
- Mitigation: customer enabled `prefer_unbatched` (done).
- SRE: investigate serializer warning + correlate to recent optimization (priya).
- ML Eng: add assertions and run local repro harness, prepare PR (jia).
- Support: coordinate canary and notify customer about billing impact (sam).

sam_support: tagging @jia_ml @priya_sre for visibility. I'll update thread with logs and PR links as they appear. :thumbsup:

daniel_acme: LGTM, standing by for fixes. Thanks all! :clap:
